column2: 古英语 sċēoh（怯）← 原始西日耳曼语 *skeuh ← 原始日耳曼语 *skeuhaz
column3: nervous about meeting or talking to others
column5: She was too shy to speak up.|The shy child hid behind her mother.
column6: drawing back from being noticed – 怕被注意而往后缩
column7: 羞怯的：见人就拘束不敢开口|畏缩的：遇事往后退不敢上前

column2: 古英语 sēoc（病）← 原始西日耳曼语 *seuk ← 原始日耳曼语 *seukaz ← 原始印欧语 *sewg-（受苦）
column3: not well in body, or wanting to vomit
column5: He stayed home sick for three days.|The smell made her feel sick.
column6: out of sound health – 身体不在健全状态
column7: 生病的：身体患病不适|恶心的：想要呕吐的

column2: 古英语 sīde（侧、胁）← 原始日耳曼语 *sīdǭ，或出原始印欧语 *seh₁-（长）
column3: one of the surfaces or edges of something, or one of two opposing groups
column5: Write your name on the other side.|Both sides agreed to talk.
column6: one face or party as against another – 相对而言的这一面或这一方
column7: 侧面：物体的一个面或边|一方：对立双方中的一边

column2: 由 side ＋ -ways 构成
column3: towards or from one side
column5: The crab moved sideways across the sand.|He glanced sideways at her.
column6: along the side rather than straight ahead – 沿侧面而非朝正前
column7: 向侧面：朝旁边的方向|侧向：从侧面来或去的

column2: 中古英语 sege ← 古法语 siege ← 俗拉丁语 *sēdicum ← 拉丁语 sēdēs（座）
column3: the surrounding of a place to force it to surrender
column5: The siege lasted almost two years.|Troops laid siege to the fort.
column6: sitting down around a place until it yields – 在一处四周坐守到它屈服
column7: 围攻：围住并进攻|包围：四面合拢困住

column2: 中古英语 sighen，由 siken 的过去式 sighte 反构而成 ← 古英语 sīcan
column3: to let out a long breath showing tiredness or relief
column5: She sighed and closed the book.|A long sigh escaped him.
column6: letting the breath out long and audibly – 长长把气放出来
column7: 叹气：出声地长长呼气|叹息：因感慨而叹

column2: 古英语 sihþ（所见）← 原始西日耳曼语 *sihti，由 see ＋ -th 构成
column3: the ability to see, or something seen
column5: His sight weakened with age.|The valley was a wonderful sight.
column6: the faculty of seeing and what it takes in – 看的能力以及所看到的东西
column7: 视力：眼睛看的能力|景象：眼前呈现的画面

column2: 由 sight ＋ seeing 复合而成
column3: visiting places of interest as a tourist
column5: They spent the day sightseeing in Rome.|Sightseeing buses leave every hour.
column6: going about to look at what is worth seeing – 四处去看值得看的东西

column2: 中古英语 silence ← 古法语 silence ← 拉丁语 silentium，源自 silēre（沉默）
column3: complete absence of sound, or refusal to speak
column5: A long silence followed the question.|She kept silence about the matter.
column6: the state of no sound being made – 没有声音发出的状态
column7: 寂静：周围没有声响|沉默：不说话不表态

column2: 借自拉丁语 silēns，为 silēre（沉默）的现在分词 ← 原始印欧语 *seyl-（静）
column3: making no sound, or choosing not to speak
column5: The room went completely silent.|He remained silent throughout the meeting.
column6: giving out no sound – 不发出声音的
column7: 无声的：不产生声响|沉默的：有意不出声

column2: 由 silicium ＋ -on 构成；silicium ← 拉丁语 silex（燧石、硅石），-on 取自 carbon
column3: a chemical element used in glass and computer chips
column5: Silicon is used in most computer chips.|The plant refines silicon for panels.
column6: the element drawn from flint-like rock – 从燧石类岩石里提取的元素

column2: 古英语 seoloc，直接来源未定，或经波罗的海商路传入 ← 晚期拉丁语 sēricus ← 希腊语 sērikos，更早出东方语言
column3: a fine soft cloth made from threads spun by silkworms
column5: She wore a scarf of pure silk.|Silk feels cool against the skin.
column6: the fine thread spun by a worm – 由蚕吐出的细纤维
column7: 丝：蚕吐出的细纤维|丝绸：用它织成的织物

column2: 古英语 sǣliġ（幸运的）← 原始西日耳曼语 *sālīg；词义由「幸运」→「无辜」→「天真」→「愚蠢」
column3: showing a lack of good sense in a harmless way
column5: That was a silly mistake to make.|He asked a silly question.
column6: lacking sense without meaning harm – 没脑筋但无恶意
column7: 傻的：反应或做法不聪明|愚蠢的：明显缺乏见识的

column2: 古英语 seolfor ← 原始西日耳曼语 *silubr ← 原始日耳曼语 *silubrą，更早词源不明
column3: a shiny white metal used for coins and jewellery
column5: The spoons are made of silver.|Silver tarnishes if left in air.
column6: the bright white metal prized since antiquity – 自古珍视的亮白金属
column7: 银：一种贵金属元素|白银：作为货币或材料的银

column2: 中古英语 simplicite ← 古法语 simplicite ← 拉丁语 simplicitās，源自 simplex（单一）
column3: the quality of being easy to understand or free of extras
column5: The design wins through sheer simplicity.|She admired the simplicity of the room.
column6: being of one fold with nothing added – 一层到底、不加附饰
column7: 简单：不复杂容易把握|朴素：不加修饰而自然

column2: 法语 simplifier，相当于 simple ＋ -ify
column3: to make something easier to do or understand
column5: They simplified the whole application process.|Try to simplify the second paragraph.
column6: reducing something to fewer folds – 把层次减到更少

column2: 中古英语 symply，由 simple ＋ -ly 构成
column3: in a plain way, or merely
column5: She explained it simply and clearly.|I simply forgot to call.
column6: in a plain manner with nothing added – 不加旁枝地
column7: 简单地：以不复杂的方式|仅仅：只不过如此

column2: 古英语 synn ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sunnju ← 原始日耳曼语 *sundijō ← 原始印欧语 *h₁es-（是）——本义近「确有其事的罪责」
column3: an act that breaks a religious law
column5: He confessed his sins to the priest.|Greed was considered a sin.
column6: a guilt truly incurred against a law – 对律法确实犯下的过错
column7: 罪过：违犯教规的行为|罪孽：所积下的罪责

column2: 借自中古法语 sincere ← 拉丁语 sincērus（纯真），由 *sem-（一同）＋ *ḱer-（生长）构成
column3: saying what one really feels
column5: She gave a sincere apology.|His thanks sounded entirely sincere.
column6: grown of one piece with no pretence – 一体长成、不掺假
column7: 真诚的：所说与所想一致|诚挚的：情意深切而不虚

column2: 古英语 singan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *singwan ← 原始日耳曼语 *singwaną ← 原始印欧语 *sengʷʰ-（吟、唱）
column3: to make musical sounds with the voice
column5: She sang two songs at the wedding.|Birds sing loudest at dawn.
column6: shaping the voice into music – 把嗓音发成乐音
column7: 唱：用嗓音发出乐音|歌唱：以歌曲形式演唱

column2: 中古英语 single ← 古法语 sengle ← 拉丁语 singulus（单个），出原始印欧语 *sem-（一）
column3: only one, or not married
column5: Not a single seat was empty.|She has stayed single by choice.
column6: standing as one and one only – 只作一个、别无第二
column7: 单个的：仅有一个|单身的：未婚或无配偶

column2: 中古英语 singuler ← 古法语 ← 拉丁语 singulāris（同类中独一），源自 singulus（单个）
column3: referring to one in grammar, or unusually notable
column5: Use the singular form after each.|She showed singular courage that day.
column6: alone of its kind – 同类里只此一个
column7: 单数的：语法上指一个|非凡的：突出得与众不同

column2: 古英语 sincan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sinkwan ← 原始日耳曼语 *sinkwaną ← 原始印欧语 *sengʷ-（落下）
column3: to go down below the surface of a liquid
column5: The stone sank straight to the bottom.|Two ships sank in the storm.
column6: going down through and under – 一路往下没进去
column7: 下沉：向下移动进入下方|沉没：整体没入水下

column2: 中古英语 sippen，来源未定；或为 suppen（饮）的变体，或出古英语 sipian（渗、浸）
column3: to drink a very small amount at a time
column5: She sipped her tea very slowly.|He took one sip and stopped.
column6: taking liquid in a little at a time – 一次只把液体取进一点
column7: 小口喝：每次只喝很少|啜饮：细细品着喝

column2: 中古英语 sir，为 sire 的非重读形 ← 古法语 sire（主人）← 拉丁语 senior（较年长的），源自 senex（年老）
column3: a polite way of addressing a man
column5: Good morning, sir, may I help you.|He addressed the officer as sir.
column6: the respectful form for an elder or superior – 对长者或上位者的敬称
column7: 先生：对男子的礼貌称呼|阁下：对有身分者的敬称

column2: 中古英语 siren ← 古法语 sereine 与拉丁语 Sīrēn ← 希腊语 Seirēn（以歌声诱人的海妖）
column3: a device that makes a loud warning sound
column5: A siren wailed somewhere behind us.|The factory siren sounded at noon.
column6: a sound that carries far and pulls attention – 传得远、把注意力拉过去的声音
column7: 警笛：警车或消防车的报警声器|汽笛：船只或工厂发声的号笛

column2: 中古英语 suster ← 古英语 sweostor ← 原始日耳曼语 *swestēr ← 原始印欧语 *swésōr；今拼法的 i 受古诺尔斯语 systir 影响
column3: a girl or woman with the same parents as another
column5: Her sister lives in another city.|The two sisters look alike.
column6: a female born of the same parents – 同父母所生的女性
column7: 姐妹：同父母所生的女性亲属|姐姐：年长于自己的那一位

column2: 古英语 sittan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sittjan ← 原始日耳曼语 *sitjaną ← 原始印欧语 *sed-（坐）
column3: to rest with the body upright on a support
column5: They sat on the low stone wall.|Please sit near the front.
column6: resting the body with weight on the seat – 把体重落在座上歇着
column7: 坐：身体落在座位上|就座：入座这个动作

column2: 中古英语 site ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 site ← 拉丁语 situs（位置），源自 sinere（放置）
column3: a place where something is or will be built
column5: They chose a site near the river.|The site opens to visitors soon.
column6: the spot where something is set down – 某物被安放的那个位置
column7: 地点：某事所在的位置|工地：正在施工的场地

column2: 由 situate ＋ -ed 构成；situate ← 中世纪拉丁语 situātus，源自拉丁语 situs（位置）
column3: placed in a particular position
column5: The house is situated beside a lake.|Their office is situated downtown.
column6: set in a particular place – 被安置在某个位置上
column7: 位于：处在某个地点|所在的：处于该位置的
